experiment.approved_task: Submit each reward-requested frame to the existing asynchronous evaluator as soon as its prediction records, CPU-accessible labels and verified identities are ready, before map-update construction/publication. Then build and publish the map update normally. Neither branch waits for the other. One ordering change, not a new evaluator, queue or GPU optimization.

hypothesis_23_recovered_tickets.evidence: late tickets with excess <= 5 ms: C2 37, E 32; C2 late-excess P25 is 4.97 ms, above the realized median saving (0.4 ms) and even above the gross 3.7 ms shift once the evaluator-thread slowdown is included

exactly_once.E: early 466 = evaluator 466, loop 0, suppressed 466, errors 0, live-gate rejections 0, non-reward frames 599

mechanism.gt_readiness: GT bundle was ready ~100 ms before the ticket in 459/460 (C2) and 466/466 (E) evaluations: the evaluator is submission-bound, never GT-bound, in both arms
mechanism.reading: the submission moved 3.7 ms earlier at the median (compute_end_to_submit 3.8 -> 0.1 ms) for every reward ticket, but the evaluator thread's probe/read/evaluate phase slowed by ~1.8 ms (submit->emit 7.65 -> 9.45 ms wall P50) while overlapping the compute thread's map build/publish in the same CPython process; realized compute_end->receipt gain is 0.4 ms P50 / 1.7 ms P95. The primary-metric improvement is dominated by ao->compute_end (P95 210.7 -> 184.6; edge compute P99 241.6 -> 109.7; edge queue P99 76.1 -> 46.6), which the ordering change cannot produce.

no_further_work: after the two captures: report and stop; no further optimization, retraining, Run-5 integration or additional captures; no push
noise_context: same-configuration cap-only captures now span 66.2% (C2), 71.4% (C), 75.2% (B): the C2->E +5.5 pt lies inside that spread; two captures do not define a noise band
recommendation: INCONCLUSIVE on the primary metric; the mechanism is verified (exactly-once early submission, map content/bytes/freshness unchanged, no regression) but its realized per-ticket gain is 0.4 ms P50 / 1.7 ms P95, far below the 3.7 ms shift and below the late-excess floor, so the ordering change is NOT retained as a timeliness improvement; the production (serial) ordering remains the live path. The next single-process bottleneck it exposes is CPython GIL sharing between the edge compute thread and the evaluator thread (post-hoc observation, not a registered result).
